title: Lighthouse Financial pilot: acceptance criteria & regression strategy
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week pilot: agree on success criteria, golden prompts and regression sets, size a benchmark workload for latency/cost targets, and map security questions (KMS, audit logs, SSO). Redwood to share benchmark template and security pack. Next: baseline tests, pilot contract, and schedule deep-dive for private deployment considerations.
action_items: Maya Chen - Share Redwood benchmark spreadsheet and pilot pricing estimate - 2026-05-18
Anil Kapoor - Draft initial golden prompts template and example outputs - 2026-05-20
Raj Patel - Provide 100 anonymized user queries for golden/regression set - 2026-05-21
Tariq Alvi - Confirm required compliance docs (SOC2 scope, encryption) and note any data residency constraints - 2026-05-19
Sophie Li - Schedule 90-min technical deep dive for private deployment options - 2026-05-22
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet + security packet
Customer to deliver sample query set and acceptance criteria matrix
Schedule private deployment deep-dive if data residency blocks hosted option
Agree final pilot timeline and sign pilot SOW
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Anil Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sophie Li (Redwood CSM), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Lighthouse Head of ML), Elena Gomez (Lighthouse Eng Manager), Tariq Alvi (Lighthouse Security), Marta Ruiz (Lighthouse Product)

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio ok for folks?
00:05 - Raj Patel: Yeah, good here. Thanks Maya.
00:07 - Elena Gomez: All good.
00:10 - Maya Chen: Great. High level — we wanted to align on what success looks like for the pilot, how we measure quality, and the workload/benchmarks so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted. We'll also cover any security blockers.
00:22 - Raj Patel: Perfect. We're primarily looking at an assistant that helps our relationship managers summarize calls and generate compliance-safe follow ups. Key constraints: latency under 250ms p95 ideally, cost under $0.002 per turn token-equivalent, and hallucination tolerances are very low because of financial risk.
00:40 - Anil Kapoor: Got it. For clarification — 250ms p95 is for end-to-end generation including any post-processing? Or model only?
00:47 - Raj Patel: Model + lightweight postprocess, yes. The RM UI is very latency sensitive.
:52 - Anil Kapoor: Ok makes sense. We'll plan to include the inference + small-formatting step in our latency targets. We'll also propose a baseline batch/kv-cash — kv cash — excuse me, KV cache strategy to hit those numbers.
01:05 - Elena Gomez: Also, we have to keep all PII out of model logs. So token logging and retention policy is a hard requirement.
01:12 - Maya Chen: Understood. Redwood supports configurable token retention and we can route logs to their VPC or customer-managed bucket for the pilot. Sophie, any notes on SOC2?
01:20 - Sophie Li: We have the latest SOC2 and ISO attestation, plus an enterprise pack with KMS integrations and audit-log retention. We'll attach those docs.
01:28 - Marta Ruiz: Timeline question — we're targeting a 6-week pilot, is that realistic?
01:33 - Maya Chen: Yes, our typical pilot is 4–8 weeks. For what you described (quality playbook + throughput benchmarks + security review) 6 weeks is reasonable. Week 0: kickoff and data handoff; Week 1–2: golden prompt and baseline benchmarks; Week 3–4: iterative tuning and regression runs; Week 5: load and SLO validation; Week 6: acceptance and next steps.
01:54 - Raj Patel: Sounds good. On golden prompts — we have domain-specific phrasing and compliance templates that need to be preserved. Can Redwood help craft the golden prompt library?
02:02 - Anil Kapoor: Absolutely. We'll provide a golden prompts template and sample prompts tailored to RM workflows. We'll also define a scoring rubric — precision, factuality, formatting correctness, and hallucination penalties. Example: if response contradicts a customer-provided fact, that's an immediate fail for that case.
02:24 - Elena Gomez: Can you expand on hallucination detection? Tools or metrics?
02:27 - Anil Kapoor: We'll use a mix — exact-match checks against ground truth where available, semantic entailment scoring for paraphrase tolerance, and a set of blacklist/format checks. Practically: each golden prompt will have an expected key-entities list and allowed templates. Any extraneous entity insertion or confident but false statements get a penalty. We'll produce both quantitative scores and sample failure categories.
02:51 - Raj Patel: For the regression suite, we need to ensure no quality regressions across model variants and quantized builds. We also plan periodic replays after infra or model upgrades.
03:00 - Dev Patel: We'll set up a CI-driven regression harness — can replay historical prompts and compare embeddings/intent drift plus hallucination flags. We'll output an HTML regression report with diffs and severity labels.
03:15 - Marta Ruiz: Nice. Can we capture user-level acceptance thresholds? For example, 95% of summaries must be rated >=3 on a 1–5 scale by a small RM panel.
03:25 - Anil Kapoor: Yes, we'll incorporate a human-eval curve. We'll seed a small internal RM panel to produce ratings for the goldset and align on acceptance thresholds. That becomes the human-grounded check along with automated metrics.
03:38 - Elena Gomez: On workload sizing — our peak concurrent RMs is about 120, but requests are bursty. Typical summary size is 200–400 tokens.
03:47 - Maya Chen: Ok, we'll map that to tokens/sec and recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable latency; hosted could work if cost and data flow are acceptable and if we use caching aggressively.
03:58 - Raj Patel: Any specifics on how Redwood recommends batching vs single-shot to keep latency low?
04:05 - Anil Kapoor: We do continuous batching with dynamic latency thresholds. For sub-250ms p95, we usually run single-shot or very small micro-batches and rely on KV cache for repeated prefixes. We'll propose a config: micro-batch max 4, pre-warming of KV for common templates, and quantized variant for cost. We'll include measured tradeoffs in the benchmark spreadsheet.
04:30 - Elena Gomez: About data residency — we need EU-only processing for EU customer data. How does Redwood handle region pinning?
04:37 - Maya Chen: We can pin model serving to specific regions, and for Private deployments we can run in your VPC or on-prem. We'll discuss the private deployment deep-dive if that is the path.
04:48 - Tariq Alvi: Security: KMS/HSM integration is mandatory; we also need proof of key separation and audit logs with retention policy. Also SSO/SAML for RBAC.
04:58 - Sophie Li: We support KMS integrations and can provide the key separation design. We'll send sample audit log schemas. For SSO, we support SAML and OIDC integrations.
05:10 - Raj Patel: Good. Back to scoring — can we see a sample rubric now?
05:15 - Anil Kapoor: Quick high-level:
 - Content Accuracy (0-5) — checks factual correctness
 - Entity Fidelity (0-5) — correct entities included, no spurious insertion
 - Formatting (0-3) — preserves required templates
 - Hallucination Flag (binary) — immediate fail if triggered for regulated fields
 - Latency (pass/fail vs target)
We'll weight them for an overall score; we'll share exact weights in the spreadsheet.
05:46 - Raj Patel: For hallucination flags — immediate fail on e.g., inventing financial advice or regulatory statements?
05:52 - Anil Kapoor: Exactly. Anything that looks like definitive regulatory guidance or fabricated statistics is fail.
05:58 - Marta Ruiz: On golden prompts selection — we can start with 40 core prompts covering RM workflows: call summary, action items, follow-up templates, compliance-safe language. We can then expand to a 200-case regression set including edge-cases.
06:12 - Dev Patel: We'll ask for a seed set of 100 anonymized historical transcripts and 40 labeled prompts to generate the golden/regression sets. Raj, is that feasible?
06:21 - Raj Patel: Yes, we can provide anonymized extracts. Security will need to approve redaction process.
06:26 - Tariq Alvi: We'll own redaction. We'll provide the sample dataset via a secure S3 share and indicate any fields that must be masked.
06:33 - Elena Gomez: Benchmarks — what does Redwood need to run an apples-to-apples latency/cost benchmark?
06:38 - Anil Kapoor: Ideally: sample prompt set (200–500 items), expected response length distribution, concurrency pattern (peak/avg), and any postprocessing steps. We'll run baseline models (open models you prefer) plus Redwood-optimized variants and return p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
06:56 - Raj Patel: We'll include target SLOs. Also need to know how to interpret model variants when quantized builds change hallucination characteristics.
07:05 - Anil Kapoor: We'll capture both quality metrics and a quantization-sensitivity report. Sometimes INT8 variants are fine for summarization but degrade entity fidelity — we'll surface that.
07:16 - Maya Chen: Quick note on reporting: we'll produce a pilot dashboard with per-prompt metrics, regression diffs, and a weekly summary.
07:25 - Elena Gomez: Great. Contractually — will Redwood require a non-prod token cap for the pilot?
07:30 - Maya Chen: Typically we'll propose a pilot cap to bound cost; we'll include that in the SOW. We can be flexible.
07:36 - Raj Patel: On acceptance — we want both automated pass rates and human-eval score thresholds. For example, 90% automated pass on hallucination checks and 95% of human-evals >=3.
07:46 - Anil Kapoor: That's reasonable. We'll codify the acceptance matrix and include edge-case severity buckets (critical, major, minor) that drive go/no-go.
07:58 - Marta Ruiz: Any constraints around model fine-tuning? We prefer prompt engineering and retrieval augmentation rather than persistent fine-tuning for now.
08:06 - Anil Kapoor: We can support both. For pilot speed, we recommend prompt engineering + retrieval + small in-context examples. Fine-tuning can be scoped if necessary.
08:16 - Elena Gomez: Ok. For the regression harness, how do you signal false positives from automated hallucination detectors? We don't want noisy alerts.
08:25 - Dev Patel: We'll tune thresholds and include an adjudication queue for human review. The regression report will flag likely hallucinations and include confidence scores. Over time the adjudication feedback reduces false positives.
08:36 - Raj Patel: Are there any typical surprises teams see in pilots?
08:38 - Maya Chen: Common ones: unexpected token inflation due to verbose prompts, context window misalignment, and subtle entity hallucinations after quantization. We try to catch those in the first regression sweep.
08:51 - Elena Gomez: For pilot acceptance, who should sign off on Lighthouse side?
08:55 - Raj Patel: I'll own ML sign-off, Elena for engineering, and Tariq for security. Those three are final approvers.
09:03 - Maya Chen: Perfect. Let's confirm concrete next steps and owners — Maya to send benchmark template & SOW draft; Anil to send golden prompt template; Raj to provide anonymized sample prompts; Tariq to confirm redaction process and compliance constraints.
09:16 - Raj Patel: We'll aim to have the sample set and redaction rules to you by May 21.
09:20 - Sophie Li: We'll also set up a pilot Slack channel and share weekly check-in cadence.
09:24 - Marta Ruiz: Can you include a short demo before week 2 so RMs can see examples?
09:28 - Anil Kapoor: Yes, we'll run a short demo showing baseline outputs and where we'll focus tuning.
09:32 - Elena Gomez: One last question — can Redwood produce a hallucination heatmap per prompt type?
09:37 - Dev Patel: Yes, that's in our regression report — per-prompt failure rates, heatmaps by entity type, and sample counterexamples.
09:45 - Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with the docs. Thanks everyone.
09:48 - Raj Patel: Thanks, see you.
09:50 - (call ends)
notes: Redwood to emphasize golden prompt control and KV/cache strategies in follow-up. Customer requires strict token retention and KMS proofing. Pilot acceptance requires combined automated+human thresholds. Possible path to private deployment if data residency or KMS concerns persist.
